The research covers:
- Why session flags (`SET default_transaction_read_only`) are safety guards, not security boundaries
- Per-database read-only role setup (PostgreSQL `pg_read_all_data`, MySQL `GRANT SELECT`, SQLite URI + authorizer callback)
- Column-level grants and view-based PII filtering
- Row-Level Security layered on top
- SQLAlchemy `postgresql_readonly=True` connection hardening
- pgBouncer routing to read replicas
- Read replicas as the strongest physical write boundary
- Stored procedures as a whitelist alternative
